en.title: Global Macro — China's orders retreat as Europe's output slows and energy risks outlast the bond rally
en.deck: China's October factory and export-order surveys fell below 50, Europe's Q3 GDP growth slowed and US yields eased; uneven demand meets persistent energy risks.

en.key_risk: Industrial demand weakens while energy import costs and borrower-specific credit costs stay elevated.

contrary_evidence: Chinese high-technology manufacturing subsectors above 53 and large manufacturers at 50.2; one-month survey can be affected by holidays.
Euro-area real GDP still expanded 0.4% q/q in Q3; Irish and Spanish growth show heterogeneity.
US Q3 real GDP rose 3.4% annualised, inconsistent with a uniform global contraction.

The US BEA reported real DPI -0.3% m/m and real PCE 0.0% for September, from its separate September Personal Income and Outlays release, not the Q3 GDP advance estimate; monthly demand weakness does not erase +3.4% annualized Q3 GDP growth.
Eurostat's preliminary Q3 2026 country data show Lithuania -1.0% and France -0.1% quarter-on-quarter despite euro-area +0.4% aggregate; Portuguese signed GDP comparison corrected to match English.
limitations: China PMI is a diffusion index and not measured export volumes, factory output growth or SME credit access.
Eurostat GDP is preliminary, country composition and annualisation differ from US GDP.
No independently verified new Gulf shipping throughput, insurance costs or borrower-level credit spreads.
Cross-border capital flow attribution unavailable; ICI money fund asset change cannot identify international reallocations.

evidence_sources.name: BEA Personal Income and Outlays September 2026
